allies.rationale_text: Experimentation helps optionality buy learning cheaply before the irreversible choice is forced.
allies.source_quote: Most useful when uncertainty is high, early commitment is expensive, and cheap experiments can buy learning before an irreversible call.
allies.affinity_rationale: Experimentation generates the options that optionality preserves — 'provides alternative pathways and allows flexibility to pursue multiple solutions simultaneously'.
allies.activation_condition: When creating valuable options requires active hypothesis testing and exploration rather than theoretical enumeration of possibilities

allies.rationale_text: Trade-offs helps optionality compare multiple paths by making the downside and sacrificed alternatives explicit instead of binary.
allies.source_quote: By generating numerous options, this mental model aims to make decision-making more effective and helps compare the upside potential against the risk of the downside potential.
allies.affinity_rationale: Optionality IS about managing trade-offs between commitment and flexibility — every option preserved has an implicit cost in commitment delayed.
allies.activation_condition: When the decision to preserve or exercise an option requires explicit evaluation of what is gained in flexibility versus what is lost in commitment and focus

allies.rationale_text: Decision-trees help optionality model branching choices and probabilistic outcomes instead of treating the future as one track.
allies.source_quote: decision trees can be used, particularly if some choices are probabilistic in nature
allies.affinity_rationale: Decision trees map the branching possibilities that optionality maintains — structured pathway analysis helps evaluate when to exercise versus preserve options.
allies.activation_condition: When the value of maintaining versus exercising options needs to be evaluated through structured analysis of branching outcomes and their probabilities

antagonists.rationale_text: Confirmation-bias shrinks optionality by locking attention onto the preferred path and filtering out superior alternatives.
antagonists.source_quote: Confirmation bias causes us to seek information that confirms an initial belief or preferred option, leading to an inability to see superior alternatives.
antagonists.affinity_rationale: Described as 'severely limiting' optionality — confirmation bias causes inability to see superior alternatives by seeking information that confirms the preferred option.
antagonists.activation_condition: When attachment to a preferred option causes selective evidence gathering that makes alternatives invisible despite their objective superiority

antagonists.rationale_text: Commitment-and-consistency-bias makes optionality psychologically expensive because prior choices become harder to revisit even when better paths appear.
antagonists.affinity_rationale: Commitment makes it 'extremely difficult to pivot or consider new, better options' — psychological pressure from prior choices directly destroys the flexibility optionality requires.
antagonists.activation_condition: When prior investment or public commitment creates escalation pressure that forecloses objectively superior alternatives because pivoting feels like failure

structured_tensions.tension_text: Optionality conflicts with commitment-bias when preserving options delays the commitment needed to capture time-sensitive value.
structured_tensions.source_quote: optionality conflicts with commitment-bias (commitment bias) when preserving options delays the commitment needed to capture time-sensitive value.

structured_tensions.tension_text: Optionality conflicts with prioritization when keeping all options open prevents the ruthless elimination that focused execution requires.
structured_tensions.source_quote: optionality conflicts with prioritization (prioritization) when keeping all options open prevents the ruthless elimination that focused execution requires.

curation_notes.summary: Layer 1+2 enrichment complete. Allies: experimentation 0.90 (strong — generates the options optionality preserves), trade-offs 0.80 (moderate — manages commitment vs flexibility), decision-trees 0.80 (moderate — structured pathway evaluation). Antagonists differentiated: confirmation-bias 0.90 (strong — 'severely limits' by hiding alternatives), commitment-bias 0.90 (strong — 'extremely difficult to pivot' — directly destroys flexibility).

open_questions: Systems-thinking is a source-real ally, but experimentation, trade-offs, and decision-trees were the cleaner bounded links into the current graph.
